title.value: Broadening the scope of anthropogenic influence in extreme event attribution

scope_reason: The perspective paper proposes an extreme-event-attribution framework and examines hazard events and their impacts through case studies (Kenyan drought, NE Pacific marine heatwave, 2017 Portugal fires, Venice Acqua Alta, California drought), including its own reservoir counterfactual analysis.

scope_quote.evidence_text: Furthermore, we provide illustrations for five case studies: the 2021-2022 Kenyan drought; the 2013-2015 marine heatwave in the northeast Pacific; the 2017 forest fires in Portugal

support_span.evidence_text: The pilot project was Lake Mendocino, a reservoir with a maximum storage of 111 000 acre-feet in the upper Russian River watershed in coastal northern California.
The stressor is the water level in Lake Mendocino (figure 6).

experimental_condition.value: FIRO-enabled extra storage (factual) versus reservoir managed to its previously mandated storage limits (counterfactual)

support_span.evidence_text: We present two versions of the water storage levels in the first FIRO pilot reservoir, one with the extra storage enabled by FIRO (factual) and another with the reservoir being managed to its previously mandated storage limits (counterfactual).

evidence.evidence_text: The water saved through the use of a major deviation, requested as a result of the positive FIRO viability assessment, was close to 20% in water year 2020 (figure 7).
